title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Delivers 2.89 Lakh Pucca Houses Worth ₹3,473 Crore to Rajasthan Under PMAY-G
subtitle:
340.59 Crore Approved for Agricultural Development and PM-RKVY; Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Hands Over Sanction Letter to CM Shri Bhajan Lal Sharma
29.13 Lakh New Beneficiaries Surveyed Under PMAY-G; More Houses to be Sanctioned After Physical Verification: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Major PMAY-G Eligibility Reforms: Two-Wheeler Owners, Women Earning Up to ₹15,000 and Small Farmers Now Eligible for Housing Support
No Woman Should Remain Poor: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Doubles Rajasthan’s Lakhpati Didi Target to 32 Lakh
Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana: ₹12,000 Crore Target for Rajasthan; Panchayats to Drive Development with Annual Goal of ₹80 Lakh Each
Urea at ₹266 a Bag for Farmers Despite ₹3,000 Cost: Government Continues to Bear the Burden, Says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Tougher Laws Against Fake Pesticides and Substandard Seeds: New Pesticide and Seed Legislation to be Introduced in Parliament, Says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
body_text:
Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, during his visit to Rajasthan today, participated in the state-level program of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin in Baran along with Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma. On the occasion, Shri Chouhan handed over to the Chief Minister the approval letter for 2,89,355 houses under PMAY-G, involving a project outlay of ₹3,473 crore. He also handed over an approval letter for ₹340.59 crore under agricultural development initiatives and the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana. The program was attended by Members of Parliament, MLAs, ministers in charge, and a large number of local residents.
PM’s Commitment to Pucca Houses for the Poor Being Fulfilled
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s commitment to providing pucca houses to poor families in Rajasthan is being fulfilled. “Today, approval is being given for 2,89,355 houses at a cost of ₹3,473 crore and this gift is being dedicated to Rajasthan. It will bring a positive transformation in the lives of families who have so far been living in kutcha houses,” he said. He added that ₹340.59 crore under various agriculture-related schemes has also been released for the development of the state.
Survey Completed for 29.13 Lakh New Beneficiaries
Shri Chouhan informed that a survey of 29,13,749 new beneficiaries has been completed. After physical verification, houses will also be sanctioned for the remaining eligible beneficiaries. He directed that transparent beneficiary lists be displayed at the district and panchayat levels, objections be heard, and wrongful exclusion of eligible beneficiaries be prevented so that deserving families do not lose their benefits due to errors.
Three Major Changes in Eligibility Rules
Shri Chouhan announced three major changes in the eligibility criteria for housing assistance. Families owning a two-wheeler will now also be eligible for a pucca house, removing the earlier restriction. Women earning up to ₹15,000 per month will also be eligible for the benefit. The earlier income ceiling was ₹10,000 per month. Small farmers owning up to 5 acres of unirrigated land or 2.5 acres of irrigated land will also be eligible for housing assistance.
Women’s Empowerment and Lakhpati Didi Mission
The Union Minister said that women’s empowerment is one of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s key priorities. He announced that 16 lakh women in Rajasthan have so far become Lakhpati Didis, and the target will now be doubled to 32 lakh Lakhpati Didis. Shri Chouhan further said that ₹13,400 crore has so far been disbursed to women through various banks to support their entrepreneurial activities.
Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana for Rural Development
Referring to the newly introduced Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana, Shri Chouhan said that Rajasthan has been given a target of ₹12,000 crore in investment over the next nine months. He said the impact of the initiative would reach every gram panchayat, with a target of providing approximately ₹80 lakh annually to each panchayat. The Union Minister made it clear that development priorities in villages would not be decided in Delhi or Jaipur. “The people themselves will decide development plans at the panchayat level,” he said.
Ensuring Fertiliser Availability and Protecting Farmers from High Costs
On the availability of urea, Shri Chouhan said the government was ensuring that farmers were not burdened by international prices. He said that although a bag of urea costs around ₹3,000, arrangements have been made to ensure that farmers receive it for only ₹266. He also assured farmers of strict action against black marketing of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs.
Strict Action Against Fake Agricultural Inputs
Shri Chouhan said that the existing legal framework is not adequate to deal with the menace of fake pesticides and substandard seeds. He announced that stronger legislation relating to pesticides and seeds would be brought in the next session of Parliament, with provisions for stringent punishment for those involved in such malpractice and stronger protection for farmers.
Agriculture Roadmap for the Kota-Jhalawar Region
Shri Chouhan said that he would work with scientists and local farmers to prepare a comprehensive agricultural roadmap for the Kota-Jhalawar region. The roadmap, he said, would focus on the entire value chain, including new crops, processing, marketing and exports, with the objective of increasing farmers’ incomes from the farm gate to global markets.
Call for Service and Collective Participation
The Union Minister praised the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the state government and called upon citizens to contribute to social causes, including serving society, planting trees, educating daughters and promoting a drug-free society. He also administered a pledge to those present and called upon everyone to work together towards building a Viksit Rajasthan and Viksit Gaon.
Vande Mataram is a symbol of India’s freedom struggle, sacrifice and patriotism: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
In his address, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that Vande Mataram is a symbol of India’s freedom struggle, sacrifice and patriotism, and that respecting it is the duty of every Indian.

enrichment.summary: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan visited Baran, Rajasthan, and handed Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma sanction letters for 2,89,355 houses (₹3,473 crore) under PMAY-Gramin and ₹340.59 crore for agricultural development/PM-RKVY. He announced three PMAY-G eligibility reforms — two-wheeler owners are now eligible, the income cap for women beneficiaries rises from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000/month, and small farmers with up to 5 acres unirrigated (2.5 acres irrigated) land now qualify. He also doubled Rajasthan's Lakhpati Didi target to 32 lakh and announced the new Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana with a ₹12,000 crore investment target for the state.
enrichment.context:
PMAY-Gramin, launched in 2016 to replace the Indira Awaas Yojana, aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to rural households living in kutcha/dilapidated houses, with cost-sharing between centre and states (90:10 for most states, 60:40 for others). Periodic revisions to eligibility criteria—such as asset ownership thresholds (vehicles, land) and income ceilings—determine who qualifies under the Socio-Economic Caste Census-based exclusion/inclusion criteria, and such reforms are significant because they can substantially expand or contract the beneficiary pool nationwide, not just in Rajasthan. The relaxation of criteria mentioned here (two-wheeler ownership, higher income ceiling for women, land-holding thresholds for small farmers) reflects a broader recalibration of the scheme's targeting norms.

The release also references Lakhpati Didi, a mission under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission framework targeting women in Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to achieve annual household income above ₹1 lakh, and the newly named 'Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana', which appears to channel panchayat-level investment (targeting roughly ₹80 lakh per panchayat annually) as part of the broader Viksit Bharat 2047 vision emphasizing decentralized, panchayat-driven development planning. The mention of upcoming pesticide and seed legislation to curb spurious agricultural inputs points to a pending legislative reform relevant to agricultural input regulation and farmer protection.

prelims_questions.question: Under recent eligibility reforms to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) as announced in August 2026, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Ownership of a two-wheeler now disqualifies a household from housing assistance
The income ceiling for women beneficiaries was raised from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 per month
Only landless agricultural labourers are eligible for the scheme
Small farmers with any amount of irrigated land are excluded from the scheme
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the earlier income ceiling of ₹10,000 per month for women has been raised to ₹15,000 per month, and that two-wheeler ownership no longer disqualifies a household, contrary to the other options.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative mentioned in the release is primarily associated with which scheme/mission?
options: Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana
prelims_questions.explanation: Lakhpati Didi is a mission targeting women in Self-Help Groups under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission framework to help households achieve an annual income above ₹1 lakh.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of periodic revisions to eligibility criteria under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin. How do such changes affect the scheme's targeting efficiency and inclusivity?
Examine the role of women-centric livelihood missions such as 'Lakhpati Didi' in advancing rural women's economic empowerment in India.

study_notes.reason: The release carries a testable factual core (specific PMAY-G eligibility revisions, cost-sharing norms, Lakhpati Didi and urea pricing figures) alongside genuine analytical material on welfare-scheme targeting design, decentralised rural planning, and gaps in farmer-input regulation, making it usable both for objective recall and for argument-building.

prelims.point: PMAY-Gramin was launched in 2016, replacing the earlier Indira Awaas Yojana, to provide pucca houses to rural households in kutcha/dilapidated dwellings.
prelims.why_important: Basic scheme lineage (predecessor scheme name and launch year) is a recurring UPSC prelims-style fact.

prelims.point: Lakhpati Didi mission, under the DAY-NRLM framework, targets women SHG members achieving annual household income above ₹1 lakh; Rajasthan's target has been doubled to 32 lakh.
prelims.why_important: Links a named mission to its parent scheme (DAY-NRLM) and its defining income threshold, both testable specifics.

prelims.point: Farmers receive a urea bag priced at about ₹266 against an actual cost of roughly ₹3,000, the difference being borne as subsidy.
prelims.why_important: The urea subsidy gap is a frequently tested fact illustrating input-subsidy mechanisms in Indian agriculture.

mains.point: The newly announced Viksit Bharat-G RAM G Yojana channels investment (~₹80 lakh per panchayat annually) with development priorities decided at the panchayat level rather than by state or central authorities.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on strengthening Panchayati Raj institutions and bottom-up planning versus top-down scheme design.

mains.point: The Minister acknowledged that existing legal provisions are inadequate to check fake pesticides and substandard seeds, necessitating new legislation with stricter penalties.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on regulatory gaps affecting farmer welfare, input quality control, and consumer protection in agriculture.

mains.point: Government subsidises urea heavily to shield farmers from international price volatility, while also facing the challenge of curbing black marketing of fertilisers.
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on fiscal sustainability of input subsidies versus need to ensure farmer access and affordability.

both.concept: Revision of PMAY-G eligibility criteria: removal of the two-wheeler ownership disqualification, raising the women's income ceiling from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000/month, and extending eligibility to small farmers with up to 5 acres unirrigated (2.5 acres irrigated) land.
both.prelims_angle: UPSC could test the specific revised thresholds (income ceiling figures, land-holding limits, asset exclusion criteria) as factual statements.
both.mains_angle: Enables analysis of how asset- and income-based means testing in welfare schemes creates inclusion/exclusion errors, and how periodic recalibration attempts to balance targeting accuracy with expanding coverage.
